title: Place & Manner
text:
Place & Manner

Place

Where the point of greatest constriction is.



Manner

What happens at that place of constriction.

title: Place & Manner
text:
Place
Most articulations have an active and a passive articulator

Active: the articulator that moves
Passive: the articulator that gets moved to

Most places of articulation are named for the location of the passive articulator.

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Ejectives

An oral closure is made.
The glottis is tightly closed.
The larynx is raised.
Pressure builds behind the oral closure.
The oral closure is released.
The built up pressure rushes out.

title: Voicing and Airstream
text: Ejectives

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Ejectives
You can have an ejective at any point of closure, and it’s transcribed with [’] (a regular apostrophe)











bilabial
alveolar
retroflex
palatal
velar
uvular




[p’]
[t’]
[ʈ’]
[c’]
[k’]
[q’]



Ejective fricatives and affricates are also possible.

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Practicing Ejectives
Try holding your breath (thus closing your glottis) and articulating “t t t t” repeatedly.

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Implosives

An oral closure is made.
The glottis is tightly closed.
The larynx lowers.
Pressure drops behind the oral closure.
The oral closure is released.
Air rushes in, normalizing the low pressure.

title: Voicing and Airstream
text: Implosives

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Implosives
Implosives can be made at any point of closure, and their IPA symbols tend to have a little hooktop.









bilabial
alveolar
velar
uvular




[ɓ]
[ɗ]
[ɠ]
[ʛ]

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Clicks

A closure is made somewhere in front of the velum.
While that closure is maintained, the tongue body moves back.
A vacuum is created between the point of closure and the velum.
The closure is released.
Air rushes in normalizing air pressure.

alveolar
retroflex
palatal
velar
uvular




[p’]
[t’]
[ʈ’]
[c’]
[k’]
[q’]



Ejective fricatives and affricates are also possible.

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Practicing Ejectives
Try holding your breath (thus closing your glottis) and articulating “t t t t” repeatedly.

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Implosives

An oral closure is made.
The glottis is tightly closed.
The larynx lowers.
Pressure drops behind the oral closure.
The oral closure is released.
Air rushes in, normalizing the low pressure.

title: Voicing and Airstream
text: Implosives

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Implosives
Implosives can be made at any point of closure, and their IPA symbols tend to have a little hooktop.









bilabial
alveolar
velar
uvular




[ɓ]
[ɗ]
[ɠ]
[ʛ]

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Clicks

A closure is made somewhere in front of the velum.
While that closure is maintained, the tongue body moves back.
A vacuum is created between the point of closure and the velum.
The closure is released.
Air rushes in normalizing air pressure.

title: Voicing and Airstream

title: Voicing and Airstream
text:
Clicks
You can only have clicks with active articulators that don’t interfere with the tongue body.










bilabial
dental
palatal
lateral
post-alveolar




[ʘ]
[ǀ]
[ǂ]
[ǁ]
[ǃ]

title: Speech Anatomy 3

Voice Quality
Vocal Fry
Almost everything you’ve heard about “vocal fry” in popular culture is bunk.

There’s nothing harmful about it.
People really only complain about women doing it, even though men also do it (Slobe 2016)
When people complain, they often also don’t correctly identify what they’re complaining about.
